parsed.rationale: Both `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) live in the same file (`WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift`) and same package (`app:iOS`), differ only in navigation direction, and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.75 — indicating roughly three-quarters of their token bodies are identical. The names are mirror-image antonyms, a strong signal that the two methods encode the same algorithm parameterized by a single direction value. Collapsing them into `navigateTheme(direction:)` removes the duplicated logic while keeping the two public call-sites readable.

specifics.proposed_action: Unify `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` into a single private helper method, e.g. `navigateTheme(direction: ThemeNavigationDirection)` where `ThemeNavigationDirection` is a two-case enum (`.previous`, `.next`), or alternatively `navigateTheme(offset: Int)` where the caller passes `-1` or `+1`. Both public entry points can then be thin one-liners that delegate to the shared helper, eliminating the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.75).
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two symbols are concrete methods on the same class in the same file — not protocols, not generics, not a subclass hierarchy, and not candidates for macro synthesis. The duplication is a classic 'direction-parameterized' pattern best resolved by introducing a direction parameter on a shared private helper. None of the named categories ('generic-parameterization' targets types/structs, 'subclass-lift' requires a class hierarchy, etc.) precisely describe collapsing two same-class sibling methods into a parameterized helper, so 'other' is the most accurate label.
